final:
# NASA's Artemis Program: Current Status

- **Artemis I & II Complete:** Artemis I (November 16, 2022) successfully tested NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and Orion spacecraft in an uncrewed flight to a polar distant retrograde lunar orbit and back [1]. Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026, carrying four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Jeremy Hansen—on a roughly 9-day crewed lunar flyby, splashing down on April 10, 2026 [2][3].

- **Artemis III Restructured as a Low-Earth-Orbit Test (targeting 2027):** In February 2026, NASA redesigned Artemis III, changing it from a Moon landing into a crewed low-Earth-orbit mission that will test rendezvous and docking between Orion and commercial lunar landers [4][5]. Led by Commander Randy Bresnik with a four-person crew named in June 2026, the mission targets 2027 and will test both SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landers [4][6].

- **Artemis IV: Now the First Crewed Lunar Landing (early 2028):** As a result of the restructuring, Artemis IV has become the program's first planned crewed lunar landing, targeted for early 2028 [5][7]. The Lunar Gateway space station was cancelled in March 2026 to streamline the program [7].

- **Technical and Programmatic Setbacks:** A helium flow issue found during a February 2026 dress rehearsal forced Artemis II's rocket back to the assembly building, delaying launch to April 2026 [3]; the more powerful SLS Block 1B rocket variant was also cancelled [10]. SpaceX's Starship must still complete around 10 orbital refueling demonstrations and low-Earth-orbit docking tests with Orion before any crewed Moon landing [11].

- **Artemis V in Early Planning:** A second crewed lunar landing (Artemis V) is anticipated by late 2028, but no crew or lander has yet been assigned [5][8].

I'll research the current status of NASA's Artemis program for you.## ARTEMIS PROGRAM STATUS – Research Notes (October 2026)

### ARTEMIS I (Completed)
- First uncrewed test flight of SLS, Orion, and ESM on November 16, 2022 [1]
- Orion sent into polar distant retrograde lunar orbit for ~6 days, then returned to Earth and landed in Pacific Ocean with parachutes [1]

### ARTEMIS II (Completed – April 2026)
- **Status:** Crewed Artemis II (lunar fly-by) mission flew on April 1, 2026 [1]
- **Crew:** Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), Jeremy Hansen (CSA astronaut) [2]
- **Mission details:** 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds; landed April 11, 2026 [2]
- **Delays:** After wet dress rehearsal on February 19, 2026, an issue was found with flow of helium in upper stage [3]; rocket rolled back to Vehicle Assembly Building to fix problem; Artemis II did not launch until April 1, 2026 [3]
- **Post-flight status:** In September 2026, Wiseman and Glover were named NASA emeritus astronauts and will advise Artemis III team [4]

### ARTEMIS III (In Preparation – Redesigned 2026)
- **Major restructure announced:** February 27, 2026 [5]
- **Mission redesignated:** Now a crewed low-Earth-orbit mission that will test rendezvous and docking between Orion and test versions of commercial human landing systems — SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon [4]
- **Timeline:** Targeted for 2027 in low Earth orbit (as of September 28, 2026) [5]
- **Crew:** Named by NASA on June 9, 2026; Randy Bresnik as Command [6] (per search results; additional crew members noted as in preparation)
- **Why changed:** Landers were not going to be ready for crew, and Orion had never docked with anything; neither Artemis I nor II carried docking system [6]

### ARTEMIS IV (First Crewed Lunar Landing)
- **Timeline:** Targeted early 2028 (as of September 28, 2026) [5]
- **Status:** In February 2026, this mission became the first planned lunar landing of the program, with planned launch date of early 2028 [7]
- **Lunar Gateway cancelled:** Lunar Gateway was cancelled in March 2026 [7]

### ARTEMIS V (Second Lunar Landing)
- **Timeline:** Anticipated by late 2028 (as of September 28, 2026) [5]
- **Status:** No crew or lander assigned [5]

### KEY TECHNICAL ISSUES & RECENT DEVELOPMENTS

**Orion Heat Shield:**
- Historical concern: Artemis 2 likely would've been delayed by a year to late 2026 if heat-shield replacement had been required [8]
- Status: No replacement needed for Artemis II (issue resolved)

**Liquid Hydrogen Leak (Feb 2026):**
- Liquid hydrogen leak found in Space Launch System's core stage [9] during dress rehearsal
- Leak increased in final minutes of rehearsal [9]

**SLS Block 1B Cancellation:**
- The more powerful SLS Block 1B rocket, in development for years, was cancelled [10]

**SpaceX Starship HLS Development:**
- SpaceX Starship must complete ~10 orbital refueling demos and LEO docking tests with Orion before any Moon landing [11]
- In April 2021, NASA awarded SpaceX $2.89 billion contract to develop Starship Human Landing System [12]
- Blue Origin filed legal protests, lost, and eventually received its own contract [12]
- **Note:** Internal SpaceX documents (Nov 2025) targeted June 2026 for first orbital refueling demo and June 2027 for uncrewed lunar landing; earliest crewed mission estimated September 2028 [13] — suggests potential timeline pressure

**Commercial Lander Selection:**
- SpaceX's Starship Human Landing System and Blue Origin's Blue Moon lander contracted for Artemis [4]; both will be tested during Artemis III

### ARTEMIS ACCORDS
- Not mentioned in current search results; further research needed if this topic is critical

### UNCERTAIN/DISPUTED POINTS
- Exact Artemis III crew roster (Randy Bresnik confirmed as Command; remaining crew details incomplete in results)
- Specific timelines dependent on SpaceX Starship readiness (currently tracked separately, showing potential 2028 slip)
- Whether additional delays may occur between now and Artemis IV/V launches

Based on web searches against current sources (as of October 18, 2026), here are the verified findings:

### **1. ARTEMIS I (Completed)**
**Claim:** "First uncrewed test flight of SLS, Orion, and ESM on November 16, 2022"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — Artemis I on November 16, 2022 was the first uncrewed test flight of the SLS, Orion, and ESM. [1]

**Claim:** "Orion sent into polar distant retrograde lunar orbit for ~6 days, then returned to Earth and landed in Pacific Ocean with parachutes"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The mission sent Orion into a polar distant retrograde lunar orbit for about six days before returning to Earth, where the capsule re-entered the atmosphere and landed in the Pacific Ocean with parachutes. [1]

---

### **2. ARTEMIS II (Completed – April 2026)**

**Claim:** "Crewed Artemis II (lunar fly-by) mission flew on April 1, 2026"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The crewed Artemis II (lunar fly-by) mission flew on April 1, 2026. [1]

**Claim:** "Crew: Reid Wiseman (Commander), Victor Glover (Pilot), Christina Koch (Mission Specialist), Jeremy Hansen (CSA astronaut)"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — Crew members: Reid Wiseman; Victor Glover; Christina Koch; Jeremy Hansen. [2]

**Claim:** "9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds; landed April 11, 2026"
- **Status:** PARTIALLY SUPPORTED WITH CORRECTION — Mission duration: 9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes and 15 seconds. [2] However, astronauts splashed down on April 10 in the Pacific Ocean [3], not April 11. **Landing date is WRONG.**

**Claim:** "After wet dress rehearsal on February 19, 2026, an issue was found with flow of helium in upper stage"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — After the "wet" dress rehearsal for Artemis II on February 19, 2026, an issue was found with the flow of helium in the upper stage. [4]

**Claim:** "rocket rolled back to Vehicle Assembly Building to fix problem; Artemis II did not launch until April 1, 2026"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The rocket was rolled back to the Kennedy Space Center's Vehicle Assembly Building to fix the problem. However, rolling back the rocket meant that Artemis II did not launch until April 1, 2026. [4]

**Claim:** "In September 2026, Wiseman and Glover were named NASA emeritus astronauts"
- **Status:** UNSUPPORTED — No web sources confirm this specific claim. Research notes cite it without attribution to verifiable sources.

---

### **3. ARTEMIS III (Restructured February 2026)**

**Claim:** "Major restructure announced: February 27, 2026"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman announced on 27 February 2026 that Artemis III will target NET 2027 and be reprofiled as a LEO crewed docking mission. [5]

**Claim:** "Now a crewed low-Earth-orbit mission that will test rendezvous and docking between Orion and test versions of commercial human landing systems — SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — Artemis III is designed to act as an operational risk-mitigation step, validating rendezvous, docking, and crew transfer procedures between the Orion spacecraft and commercial Human Landing System (HLS) vehicles before attempting a lunar landing on Artemis IV. [5]

**Claim:** "Timeline: Targeted for 2027 in low Earth orbit (as of September 28, 2026)"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The future Artemis III (Earth orbit) is planned for late 2027. [1]

**Claim:** "Crew: Named by NASA on June 9, 2026; Randy Bresnik as Command"
- **Status:** PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — NASA officially announces the four-member crew of Randy Bresnik, Luca Parmitano, Andre Douglas, and Frank Rubio on 09 June 2026. [5] Crew announcement confirmed; Randy Bresnik confirmed as command (implied by listing first).

**Claim:** "Landers were not going to be ready for crew, and Orion had never docked with anything; neither Artemis I nor II carried docking system"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The first Orion to fly with a docking system installed will be used on Artemis III. [6] This implicitly confirms that neither earlier Orion (Artemis I and II) carried a docking system.

---

### **4. ARTEMIS IV (First Crewed Lunar Landing)**

**Claim:** "Timeline: Targeted early 2028 (as of September 28, 2026)"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — The mission is planned for early 2028. [7]

**Claim:** "In February 2026, this mission became the first planned lunar landing of the program, with planned launch date of early 2028"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — In February 2026, this mission became the first planned lunar landing of the program, with a planned launch date of early 2028, and the Lunar Gateway was cancelled in March 2026. [7]

**Claim:** "Lunar Gateway was cancelled in March 2026"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — the Lunar Gateway was cancelled in March 2026. [7]

---

### **5. ARTEMIS V**

**Claim:** "Timeline: Anticipated by late 2028 (as of September 28, 2026)"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — Artemis V (lunar landing) for late 2028. [1]

**Claim:** "Status: No crew or lander assigned"
- **Status:** SUPPORTED — Artemis V, a further lunar surface mission with no crew or lander assigned, is anticipated by late 2028 (all targets as of September 28, 2026). [8]

- **Artemis I & II Complete:** Artemis I (November 2022) successfully tested NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) and Orion spacecraft in an uncrewed lunar orbit flight [1]. Artemis II flew on April 1, 2026, carrying four astronauts—Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Jeremy Hansen—on a 9-day crewed lunar flyby that landed April 11, 2026 [2][3].

- **Artemis III Restructured as Low-Earth-Orbit Test (2027):** NASA redesigned Artemis III in February 2026 to become a crewed low-Earth-orbit mission testing rendezvous and docking with commercial lunar landers rather than an immediate Moon landing [4][5]. Led by Commander Randy Bresnik, the mission targets 2027 and will test both SpaceX's Starship HLS and Blue Origin's Blue Moon landers [4][6].

- **Artemis IV: First Crewed Lunar Landing (Early 2028):** Following the restructure, Artemis IV is now targeted as the program's first crewed lunar landing, planned for early 2028 [5][7]. The Lunar Gateway station was cancelled in March 2026 to streamline the program [7].

- **Technical Challenges and Program Changes:** A liquid hydrogen leak delayed Artemis II's launch by two months (to April 2026), and the more powerful SLS Block 1B rocket was cancelled [3][9][10]. SpaceX's Starship must complete approximately 10 orbital refueling demonstrations and conduct low-Earth-orbit docking tests with Orion before any crewed Moon landing can occur [11].

- **Artemis V in Planning:** A second lunar landing (Artemis V) is anticipated by late 2028, though crew and lander assignments remain pending [5].
